'''Hans Adolph Rademacher''' ({{IPA|de|ˈʁaːdəmaxɐ|lang}}; 3 April 1892 – 7 February 1969) was a [[Germany|German]]-born American [[mathematician]], known for work in [[mathematical analysis]] and [[number theory]].

==Biography==
Rademacher received his Ph.D. in 1916 from [[Georg-August-Universität Göttingen]]; [[Constantin Carathéodory]] supervised his dissertation.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=7518|name=Hans Rademacher}}.</ref> In 1919, he became ''[[privatdozent]]'' under [[Constantin Carathéodory]] at [[University of Berlin]]. In 1922, he became an assistant professor at the [[University of Hamburg]], where he supervised budding mathematicians like [[Theodor Estermann]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Theodor Estermann - Biography |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Estermann/ |access-date=2022-08-24 |website=Maths History |language=en}}</ref> He was dismissed from his position at the [[University of Breslau]] by the [[Nazi]]s in 1933 due to his public support of the [[Weimar Republic]],<ref>{{Cite book|title=Mathematicians fleeing from Nazi Germany: individual fates and global impact|url=https://archive.org/details/mathematiciansfl00rsie|url-access=limited|first=Reinhard|last=Siegmund-Schultze|publisher=Princeton University Press|year=2009|isbn=978-0-691-14041-4|page=[https://archive.org/details/mathematiciansfl00rsie/page/n97 69]}}.</ref> and emigrated from Europe in 1934.

After leaving Germany, he moved to [[Philadelphia]] and worked at the [[University of Pennsylvania]] until his retirement in 1962; he held the [[Thomas A. Scott Professorship of Mathematics]] at Pennsylvania from 1956 to 1962. Rademacher had a number of well-known students, including [[George Andrews (mathematician)|George Andrews]], [[Paul T. Bateman]], [[Theodor Estermann]] and [[Emil Grosswald]].

==Research==
Rademacher performed research in [[analytic number theory]], mathematical [[genetics]], the [[Real analysis|theory of functions of a real variable]], and [[Quantum mechanics|quantum theory]]. Most notably, he developed the theory of [[Dedekind sum]]s. In 1937 Rademacher discovered an exact convergent series for the [[partition function (number theory)|partition function]] P(n), the number of integer partitions of a number, improving upon [[Ramanujan]]'s asymptotic non-convergent series and validating Ramanujan's supposition that an exact series representation existed.

==Awards and honors==
With his retirement from the [[University of Pennsylvania]], a group of mathematicians provided the seed funding for The Hans A. Rademacher Instructorships, and honored him with an honorary degree as Doctor of Science.

Rademacher is the co-author (with [[Otto Toeplitz]]) of the popular mathematics book ''The Enjoyment of Mathematics'', published in German in 1930 and still in print.<ref>''[https://www.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/the-enjoyment-of-math The Enjoyment of Math] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230326120957/https://www.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/the-enjoyment-of-math |date=2023-03-26 }}'' Review by Allen Stenger, [[Mathematical Association of America]]</ref><ref>{{cite journal
 | last = Oakley | first = C. O.

 | doi = 10.2307/2308857
 | issue = 8
